Deduplicate sampled history/positive/negative IDs with `unique_ids, inverse = torch.unique(ids, return_inverse=True)`, encode each unique item once, then reconstruct occurrences using `encoded[inverse]` before computing the original loss. Autograd accumulates repeated uses; do not detach reconstructed embeddings or average the loss over unique items. This preserves deterministic encoder gradients, but encoder dropout becomes shared across repeated items; apply occurrence-level dropout after reconstruction if needed. Preserve regularization explicitly: full-table penalties stay full-table; occurrence-weighted penalties require reconstructed embeddings or occurrence counts and the original denominator. AdamW decay is a separate operation, not an interchangeable replacement. `scale_grad_by_freq=True` changes behavior after deduplication, and `max_norm` mutates embedding weights during forward. These implementation implications follow from PyTorch’s [unique mapping](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.unique.html), [embedding semantics](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/sparse.py), and [AdamW definition](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html).

For full-catalog inference, encode candidate IDs in bounded chunks using the same jointly trained token-pooling/fusion network used during sampled training. Score chunks and maintain global top-k to avoid materializing every user–catalog score; apply unseen-item and padding masks consistently. Engineering recommendation: build a fused-embedding cache only after loading the selected checkpoint, calling `model.eval()`, and entering `torch.inference_mode()`. Invalidate it after any parameter update, checkpoint reload, or change to tokenization, metadata, dtype, or device. Never reuse detached cached vectors during training. PyTorch explicitly requires evaluation mode separately from inference mode and restricts inference tensors’ later use in autograd. Cache only item-dependent representations; context-dependent features must be recomputed. See [inference-mode documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html).
